stem: Dunmore Analytics keeps three VPCs today that all need direct, low-cost connectivity to each other, and separately wants inter-VPC traffic that stays inside one Availability Zone to avoid a per-gigabyte data-transfer charge. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Build a Transit Gateway hub for the three VPCs
Create VPC peering connections between the three VPCs
Keep the peered resources that exchange the most traffic in the same Availability Zone
Route inter-VPC traffic through a shared internet-egress device across all three VPCs
Attach the three VPCs to each other through a cross-Region Transit Gateway peering connection

rationale: VPC peering gives three VPCs direct, low-cost connectivity without a hub's per-attachment and per-GB charges. Keeping same-Availability-Zone traffic between the peered resources qualifies it for the free same-AZ data transfer over the peering connection. A Transit Gateway hub adds per-attachment-hour and per-GB charges that a simple three-VPC peering mesh does not need. A shared internet-egress device is for outbound internet access, not inter-VPC traffic, and adds its own processing charge. Cross-Region Transit Gateway peering adds inter-Region charges, the opposite of the same-AZ-free goal.
